title: Pediatric Second Doses and Additional Immunocompromised Doses — Immunization Services Decision Table
content:
Two Immunization Services figures add a dose beyond the doses in the series: a pediatric second influenza dose for a young child with fewer than two lifetime doses, and an additional dose in the same season for a patient who attests being immunocompromised. The table gives both figures for every vaccination.

| Vaccination | Highest age for a pediatric second dose this season | Days between the two pediatric doses | Additional dose for an immunocompromised patient allowed | Days from the previous dose to an additional dose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seasonal Influenza Standard-Dose Vaccination | 8 | 28 | No | 0 |
| Seasonal Influenza High-Dose Vaccination | 0 (not applicable) | 0 | No | 0 |
| COVID-19 Updated Vaccination | 0 (not applicable) | 0 | Yes | 60 |
| RSV Older Adult Vaccination | 0 (not applicable) | 0 | No | 0 |
| Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccination | 0 (not applicable) | 0 | No | 0 |
| Recombinant Zoster Two-Dose Series | 0 (not applicable) | 0 | No | 0 |
| Hepatitis B Three-Dose Series | 0 (not applicable) | 0 | No | 0 |

## Decision points

**Pediatric second dose.** The highest age is in whole years: a child aged no more than that age who has fewer than two lifetime doses needs a second dose this season. Only the Seasonal Influenza Standard-Dose Vaccination carries a figure (8 years); the two pediatric doses are at least 28 calendar days apart. A figure of 0 means the pediatric second dose does not apply.

| Hypothetical child, Seasonal Influenza Standard-Dose Vaccination | Age 8 or younger? | Fewer than two lifetime doses? | Second dose this season |
|---|---|---|---|
| Age 6, one lifetime dose | Yes | Yes | Needed |
| Age 8, no lifetime dose | Yes | Yes | Needed |
| Age 9, one lifetime dose | No | Yes | Not needed under this figure |
| Age 5, two lifetime doses | Yes | No | Not needed under this figure |

**Additional immunocompromised dose.** Only the COVID-19 Updated Vaccination allows an additional dose in the same season for a patient who attests being immunocompromised; that dose is at least 60 calendar days after the previous dose. For every other vaccination the answer is No and the day figure is 0.
